usageNotes: Use this as a discovery call to list the available resource-mapping types (e.g., 'dir', 'pci', 'usb') supported by the cluster. No parameters are required and no special privileges are needed — any authenticated user or API token can call it. The returned array of objects each contain a 'name' field that corresponds to a child endpoint under /cluster/mapping/{name}.

examples.summary: List all cluster mapping resource types

tips: The response acts as an index — each returned 'name' value is a valid path segment for deeper mapping endpoints like /cluster/mapping/dir or /cluster/mapping/pci.
This endpoint is safe to poll repeatedly; it is read-only and has no side effects.
API tokens are accepted (allowtoken: true), making this suitable for automation scripts that enumerate available resource types before querying specific mappings.
